dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For two n by n real matrices X and Y, LocalDef001 X Y i j is the finite sum over all k in Fin n of |X(i,k)| |Y(k,j)|. Thus it is the (i,j)-entry of the product of the entrywise absolute-value matrices |X| and |Y|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With X=L and Y=U, this supplies the nonnegative quantity S(i,j)=sum_k |L(i,k)| |U(k,j)| appearing in every error bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For two n by n real matrices X and Y, LocalDef002 X Y i j is the finite sum over all k in Fin n of X(i,k)Y(k,j), namely the usual exact matrix-product entry (XY)(i,j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With X=L and Y=U, it makes the residual in the hypothesis equal to (LU)(i,j)-A(i,j), and the conclusion requires the exact matrix identity LU=A+DeltaA.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, possibly zero.
u is an arbitrary real number.
A, L, and U are arbitrary n by n real matrices, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
hypotheses: For every i,j in Fin n, |(LU)(i,j)-A(i,j)| <= (real(i.val) u) S(i,j), where (LU)(i,j)=sum over k in Fin n of L(i,k)U(k,j), and S(i,j)=sum over k in Fin n of |L(i,k)||U(k,j)|.
conclusions: There exists an n by n real matrix DeltaA.
The exact matrix identity LU=A+DeltaA holds pointwise.
For every i,j in Fin n, |DeltaA(i,j)| <= (real(i.val) u) S(i,j).
For every i,j in Fin n, |DeltaA(i,j)| <= (real(n-1) u) S(i,j), where n-1 is natural-number subtraction truncated at zero.
mathematical_definitions: Fin n is the zero-based index set {0,1,...,n-1} when n>0 and is empty when n=0.
(LU)(i,j) := sum_{k in Fin n} L(i,k)U(k,j), the exact ordinary matrix product.
S(i,j) := sum_{k in Fin n} |L(i,k)||U(k,j)|, equivalently the (i,j)-entry of |L||U|.
The scalar i.val is cast from a natural number to a real number.
The expression n-1 is computed in Nat, so it means max(n-1,0), and is then cast to a real number.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every dimension n, every nonnegative real u, and all real n by n matrices A, L, and U, suppose each entry of the exact residual LU-A is bounded in absolute value by the zero-based row index i times u times sum_k |L(i,k)||U(k,j)|. Then there is a perturbation matrix DeltaA such that LU=A+DeltaA exactly, each entry of DeltaA satisfies that same row-dependent bound, and each entry also satisfies the uniform bound obtained by replacing i with the truncated predecessor n-1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Only square n by n real matrices are represented.

The row coefficient is the zero-based value i.val, not i.val+1. Consequently, whenever n>0, the hypothesis forces the entire first row of LU-A to be exactly zero, and the conclusion forces the first row of DeltaA to be zero.
When n=0, Fin n is empty. All entrywise hypotheses and conclusions are vacuous, and equality and existence concern only functions on empty index domains.
When n=1, both i.val and n-1 are zero, so the hypothesis requires LU=A exactly and the perturbation must be zero.
The second bound uses natural-number subtraction before casting: n-1 is zero at n=0 rather than negative one.
The bounds are entrywise scalar absolute-value bounds. No vector norm, matrix norm, componentwise matrix-order assertion, or aggregate error measure is present.
A, L, and U are completely arbitrary. No triangularity of L or U, nonsingularity, factorization-algorithm behavior, or relationship other than the stated residual bound is assumed.

The proposition uses exact real arithmetic and exact finite sums. It contains no floating-point datatype, rounding operation, unit-roundoff semantics, or notion that A, L, U, or LU were computationally produced.
The only restriction on u is u>=0; no upper bound such as u<1 or a dimension-dependent smallness condition is encoded.
The identity LU=A+DeltaA determines DeltaA pointwise as LU-A, so the existential witness is mathematically unique despite being stated existentially.
The quantity S(i,j) is a sum of termwise absolute products and is nonnegative; it is generally not equal to |(LU)(i,j)|.
